sentences.en: People often complain that plastics are too durable.
sentences.zh: 人们经常抱怨塑料制品过于耐用。

sentences.en: Water bottles, shopping bags, and other trash litter the planet, from Mount Everest to the Mariana Trench, because plastics are everywhere and don’t break down easily.
sentences.zh: 水瓶、购物袋以及其他垃圾遍布整个星球，从珠穆朗玛峰到马里亚纳海沟，因为塑料无处不在，且不易降解。

sentences.en: But some plastic materials change over time.
sentences.zh: 但有些塑料材料会随着时间而发生变化。

sentences.en: They crack and frizzle.
sentences.zh: 它们会开裂、卷曲变形。

sentences.en: They “weep” out additives.
sentences.zh: 它们会“析出”添加剂。

sentences.en: They melt into sludge.
sentences.zh: 它们会融化成泥状物。

sentences.en: All of which creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都给博物馆等致力于保存重要文化物品的机构带来了巨大的麻烦。

sentences.en: The variety of plastic objects at risk is dizzying: early radios, avant-garde sculptures, celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.
sentences.zh: 面临风险的塑料物品种类之多令人眼花缭乱：早期的收音机、先锋派雕塑、迪士尼电影中赛璐珞动画的剧照、第一颗人造心脏。

sentences.en: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn’t always know how to mix ingredients properly, says Thea van Oosten, a polymer chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 聚合物化学家西娅·范·奥斯坦表示，某些文物尤其脆弱，因为一些塑料艺术的先驱们并不总是知道如何恰当地配比原料。范·奥斯坦在荷兰文化遗产局工作了几十年，几年前才退休。

sentences.en: “It’s like baking a cake: If you don’t have exact amounts, it goes wrong,” she says.
sentences.zh: 她说：“这就像烤蛋糕：如果分量不精确，就会出问题。”

sentences.en: “The object you make is already a time bomb.”
sentences.zh: “你制作出的物品本身就已经是一枚定时炸弹。”

sentences.en: And sometimes, it’s not the artist’s fault.
sentences.zh: 而有时候，这并非艺术家的过错。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, the Italian artist Piero Gilardi began to create hundreds of bright, colorful foam pieces.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代，意大利艺术家皮耶罗·吉拉尔迪开始创作数百件色彩鲜艳的泡沫塑料作品。

sentences.en: Those pieces included small beds of roses and other items as well as a few dozen “nature carpets”—large rectangles decorated with foam pumpkins, cabbages, and watermelons.
sentences.zh: 这些作品包括小型的玫瑰床以及其他物品，还有几十块“自然地毯”——用泡沫塑料做成的南瓜、卷心菜和西瓜装饰的大块长方形地毯。

sentences.en: He wanted viewers to walk around on the carpets—which meant they had to be durable.
sentences.zh: 他希望参观者在地毯上行走，这意味着这些地毯必须经久耐用。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，他所使用的聚氨酯泡沫本身就不稳定。

sentences.en: It’s especially vulnerable to light damage, and by the mid-1990s, Gilardi’s pumpkins, roses, and other figures were splitting and crumbling.
sentences.zh: 它尤其容易受到光线损害，到20世纪90年代中期，吉拉尔迪的南瓜、玫瑰等作品已经开始开裂、碎裂。

sentences.en: Museums locked some of them away in the dark.
sentences.zh: 博物馆将其中一些作品锁进暗处保存。

sentences.en: So van Oosten and her colleagues worked to preserve Gilardi’s sculptures.
sentences.zh: 因此，范·奥斯坦和她的同事们致力于保存吉拉尔迪的雕塑作品。

sentences.en: They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals.
sentences.zh: 他们向部分作品注入稳定和加固用的化学药剂。

sentences.en: Van Oosten calls those chemicals “sunscreens” because their goal was to prevent further light damage and rebuild worn polymer fibers.
sentences.zh: 范·奥斯坦将这些化学药剂称为“防晒霜”，因为其目的是防止进一步的光损害并修复受损的高分子纤维。

sentences.en: She is proud that several sculptures have even gone on display again, albeit sometimes beneath protective cases.
sentences.zh: 令她自豪的是，几件雕塑作品甚至得以重新展出，尽管有时是放在保护罩之下。

sentences.en: Despite success stories like van Oosten’s, preservation of plastics will likely get harder.
sentences.zh: 尽管有范·奥斯坦这样成功的先例，塑料制品的保存工作仍可能会变得更加困难。

sentences.en: Old objects continue to deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 旧物件会继续劣化。

sentences.en: Worse, biodegradable plastics, designed to disintegrate, are increasingly common.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，那些被设计成可降解的塑料制品正变得越来越常见。

sentences.en: And more is at stake here than individual objects.
sentences.zh: 而且，这里所涉及的利害关系远不止某一件物品。

sentences.en: Joana Lia Ferreira, an assistant professor of conservation and restoration at the NOVA School of Science and Technology, notes that archaeologists first defined the great material ages of human history—Stone Age, Iron Age, and so on—after examining artifacts in museums.
sentences.zh: 新里斯本大学科技学院文物保护与修复助理教授若阿纳·利娅·费雷拉指出，考古学家正是在考察了博物馆中的文物之后，才首次界定了人类历史上的重大材料时代——石器时代、铁器时代等。

sentences.en: We now live in an age of plastic, she says, “and what we decide to collect today, what we decide to preserve … will have a strong impact on how in the future we’ll be seen.”
sentences.zh: 她说：“我们现在生活在一个塑料的时代，我们今天决定收藏什么、决定保存什么……将对未来世人如何看待我们产生深远影响。”

questions.stem: According to Paragraph 1, museums are faced with difficulties in ______.
questions.analysis: 首段末句指出：种类繁多的塑料制品正面临损毁风险，让博物馆等机构“头疼不已”（creates huge headaches for institutions, such as museums, trying to preserve culturally important objects），即维护塑料展品困难。

questions.stem: Van Oosten believes that certain plastic objects are ______.
questions.analysis: 第二段 van Oosten 称早期塑料艺术先驱“并非总能正确配比原料”，好比做蛋糕量错就会失败，说明某些塑料物件先天存在缺陷。

questions.stem: Museums stopped exhibiting some of Gilardi’s artworks to ______.
questions.analysis: 第四段提到 Gilardi 的泡沫作品对光尤为脆弱，90 年代中期开裂破碎，博物馆把它们锁进暗处，即停止展出以防进一步损坏。

questions.stem: The author thinks that preservation of plastics is ______.
questions.analysis: 末两段指出塑料保存“只会更难”（will likely get harder），可降解塑料日益普遍使情况更糟，可见作者认为保存塑料有挑战。

questions.stem: In Ferreira’ s opinion, preservation of plastic artifacts ______.

options.C: will help us separate the material ages
options.D: has an impact on today’s cultural life

questions.analysis: 最后一段 Ferreira 指出考古学家正是在考察馆藏文物后定义了人类历史上的材料时代；我们如今收集和保存什么将影响后世如何看我们，说明保存塑料文物具有深远的历史意义。
